tips.text: Taebaek refers to the Han people's holy Baekdu mountain and Venus that lights the day early in the morning.
The progress line of Taebaek Pumsae, which represents the will of Venus to light the whole world through Taekwondo, is the character Gom, which means artisan.
We will now take a look at the key moves of Taebaek Pumsae.
Taebaek Pumsae consists of five key moves, namely Bomseogi Sonnal Arae Haecheomagi, Sonnal Oppo Japgi, Geumgang Pakkatmakgi, Turobaegi, and Deungjumeok Pakkachigi.
We will now take a closer look at each of the key moves of Taebaek Pumsae.
When performing Bomseogi Sonnal Arae Haecheomagi, both hands should be placed in the center line of the thigh of the front leg.
The back of your hands should each face outward and the space between your hand and body should be about one hand's length sideways.
should be about one hand's length sideways
Start in front of your chest and perform Haecheomagi downward.
When assuming postures where the legs are spread forwards and backwards like Bomseogi and Apgubi,
the arm on the same side as the front foot should cross from the outside.
For Sonnal Oppo Japgi, assume an opponent has hold of you.
Twist the thumb of the hand being held outside.
Then open your hand so the palm is seen from above.
Raise your hand and pull it close to your body to release your wrist.
Open your arm inside out and cover the back of the hand of your opponent.
Hold, bend back, and pull.
While bending and twisting, be careful not to let your elbow rise excessively or move outward
as you can only exert force effectively when the elbow is close to the torso.
For Geumgang Bakalmaki, start with Jangun Doljakui and move together to the center line.
This is a technique where the outer arm performs Olgulmaki
and the inner arm performs Anpalmok Bakalmaki at the same time.
Turoppegi is a technique where you spin the thumb toward the inner wrist
and release between an opponent's thumb and index finger.
When performing Olgulpakachigi, strengthen the shoulder and shoulder blade
by bending the elbow and utilize the torque of the torso.
The elbow should face downward and the fist raised level with the temple.
Be careful not to bend the elbow.
These are the five key moves of Taebaek Pumsae.

Cautions for Taebaek first part, taking a closer look.
Be mindful of the inner and outer location of the arm when starting Hechomaki.
During Aptagi, with the upper body fixed in place,
do not kick using only the legs.

When performing Jeppipumanchigi,
do not twist the torso excessively and lose balance or swerve to the right.

When performing Dangyojirugi,
the hammer fist being pulled must not touch the front of the opposite shoulder.
Pull the left foot to the inside of the right knee.
Move your center to the right foot.
Then complete Orenhakdariseogi Orenjageundoljageui.
When performing Wenyopchagi Orenpalgupyojeokchigi,
leave the right fist on the back in the Jageundoljageui posture.
The left fist should start from the waist and draw a circle inside out to perform the Yeopchagi.
Your arms and legs should be parallel above and below.
Cautions for Taebaek second part, taking a closer look.
When performing Geumgangbakkatmakgi, do not block after crossing your arms.
Be careful not to let the Dangyojirugi become Chijirugi.
Do not perform Jirugi while the opposite arm is fixed.
When pulling the left foot from the Orendikgupy while performing Orenjageundoljageui,
be careful not to straighten the supporting right knee.
It is important to maintain the same elevation.
During Wenyopchagi Orenpalgupyojeokchigi,
do not perform Yeopchagi by crossing your arms in front of your chest.

When performing Seongkutsewojirugi,
keep the index, middle and ring finger in a straight line at the same length to prevent injuries.
The force is concentrated in the tip of the hand with a small area of contact,
making it effective in attacking the opponent's pressure points.

Kawimaki is a technique to perform Aremaki and Anpalmokbakkatmaki simultaneously,
but it can also be utilized as a more appropriate technique depending on the motion.
Cautions for Taebaek 4th part, taking a closer look.
The basics of Kawimaki is to perform Aremaki with the left arm when the left foot is in front,
and Anpalmokbakkatmaki with the right arm.
When performing Aptagi,
be careful not to let the kicking leg pass the supporting leg and do a folding kick.
